ingredients: basmati rice, chicken, yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, biryani masala, green chilies, mint leaves, coriander leaves, onions, lemon, ghee, oil, salt
steps: Step 1 (Prep & Wash): Wash 500g chicken thoroughly. Marinate with 1/2 cup smoothly beaten thick yogurt, 1.5 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tbsp biryani masala, 1 tsp turmeric, 1.5 tsp red chili powder, juice of 1/2 lemon, and 1 tsp salt. Mix thoroughly and refrigerate for at least 1 to 2 hours for softening. Step 2 (Marinate / Mix): Wash 2 cups aged Basmati rice gently under cold water until the water runs clear. Soak in plenty of water for 30 minutes. In a large pot, bring 8 cups of water to a fast boil with whole spices (2 bay leaves, 4 cloves, 2 green cardamoms, 1-inch cinnamon stick) and 1 tbsp salt. Step 3 (Cook on Low Heat): Add the soaked, drained rice to boiling water and cook uncovered on high flame for exactly 5-6 minutes until 70% cooked (the grain should break into 3 pieces when pressed between fingers). Drain immediately in a strainer. Step 4 (Fry Onions & Spices): Heat 3 tbsp oil and 1 tbsp ghee in a wide heavy-bottomed cooking pot or biryani pot. Fry 2 thinly sliced large onions on medium heat with a pinch of salt until deep golden brown and crispy. Remove half the fried onions and set aside for layering. Step 5 (Fry Onions & Spices): In the same pot with remaining onions, add the marinated chicken along with 3 slit green chilies and half of chopped mint and coriander leaves. Cook on high heat for 6-8 minutes, stirring continuously until the chicken is sealed and releases its juices. Step 6 (Fry Onions & Spices): Lower flame to minimum. Evenly spread the chicken at the bottom. Layer the 70% cooked flavorful rice on top of the chicken. Scatter the reserved golden fried onions, fresh chopped mint leaves, coriander, 2 tbsp saffron-infused warm milk, and 1 tbsp melted ghee across the rice layer. Step 7 (Cook on Low Heat): Seal the pot tightly with aluminum foil or kneaded wheat dough, then place a heavy lid on top. Cook on low heat for 20-25 minutes (or place the pot on a preheated heavy iron tawa on low flame to prevent burning). Step 8 (Finish & Serve): Turn off heat and allow the biryani to rest without stirring for 10 minutes. Gently fluff with a flat spoon from the bottom up to mix layers without breaking rice grains. Serve piping hot with onion-cucumber raita and Mirchi ka Salan.

ingredients: mutton, gongura leaves, onions, tomatoes, ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, mustard seeds, cumin seeds, curry leaves, oil, salt
steps: Step 1 (Prep & Wash): Clean 500g mutton thoroughly. In a pressure cooker, add mutton, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, and 1/2 cup water. cook in pressure cooker on medium flame for 5-6 cooker whistles until meat is 80% tender and soft and juicy. Step 2 (Heat & Fry): Pick 2 large bunches of red-stem gongura (sorrel) leaves, wash thoroughly, and drain. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pan, add the leaves with 4 slit green chilies and a splash of water. Cook on low-medium flame for 5-6 minutes until leaves wilt and turn soft. Coarsely mash using a wooden pestle or pulse in a blender for 2 seconds. Step 3 (Fry Onions & Spices): Heat 2 tbsp oil in a heavy-bottomed pan. Add 1/2 tsp mustard seeds, 1/2 tsp cumin seeds, and a sprig of fresh curry leaves. When they crackle, add 2 finely chopped medium onions and saute until soft and pink and golden. Step 4 (Fry Onions & Spices): Add 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and saute for 1 minute until raw aroma goes away. Add 2 chopped tomatoes, 1.5 tbsp spicy Andhra red chili powder, 1 tbsp coriander powder, and 1/2 tsp garam masala. Cook on medium heat until tomatoes break down and oil separates from the edges. Step 5 (Cook on Low Heat): Pour in the cooked mutton along with its rich broth. Bring to a boil and cook on low heat for 6-8 minutes on medium flame. Stir in the mashed gongura paste, mixing thoroughly to blend the sour and savory notes. Step 6 (Finish & Serve): Cover and cook on low heat on low heat for 10-12 minutes until gravy turns thick and dark, and meat absorbs the tangy flavor. In a small ladle, heat 1 tsp ghee with 2 crushed garlic cloves and dried red chilies, pour over the curry, and serve hot with steamed rice and ghee.

ingredients: prawns, onions, tomatoes, ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder, coriander powder, turmeric, mustard seeds, cumin seeds, curry leaves, oil, salt
steps: Step 1 (Prep & Wash): Peel, clean the black thread from, and thoroughly clean 400g fresh medium prawns. Toss with 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1/2 tsp salt, and 1 tsp lemon juice; let sit for 10 minutes to eliminate any raw odor. Step 2 (Heat & Fry): Heat 2.5 tbsp peanut oil in a thick pan on medium flame. Add 1/2 tsp mustard seeds, 1/2 tsp cumin seeds, and 10 fresh curry leaves. Add 2 finely chopped large onions and saute until light golden brown. Step 3 (Fry Onions & Spices): Stir in 1.5 tbsp freshly ground ginger-garlic paste and 2 slit green chilies; saute for 90 seconds until fragrant. Add 2 finely chopped ripe tomatoes and cook until soft and oil begins to glisten. Step 4 (Fry Onions & Spices): Add 1.5 tbsp Andhra red chili powder, 1 tbsp coriander powder, 1/2 tsp roasted cumin powder, and salt to taste. Saute the spices on low flame for 1 minute without burning. Step 5 (Cook on Low Heat): Add the marinated prawns into the masala. Toss on medium-high heat for 3 minutes until prawns curl into 'C' shapes and release natural juices. Pour in 1/2 cup warm water, cover, and cook on low heat on medium-low heat for 6-8 minutes (do not overcook prawns to keep them tender and juicy). Step 6 (Finish & Serve): Remove lid and cook on medium flame until gravy thickens into a glossy semi-dry curry (iguru). top with fresh freshly chopped coriander leaves and serve hot with steamed rice.

ingredients: fish pieces, tamarind, onions, tomatoes, red chili powder, turmeric, mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds, curry leaves, oil, salt
steps: Step 1 (Prep & Wash): Clean 500g freshwater fish steaks (Rohu or Katla) with crystal salt and turmeric; rinse and drain. Soak a lemon-sized ball of aged tamarind in 1.5 cups warm water for 15 minutes and extract thick, smooth pulp. Step 2 (Heat & Fry): Heat 3 tbsp sesame (gingelly) oil in an earthen clay pot (chatti) on medium flame. Add 1/2 tsp mustard seeds, 1/4 tsp fenugreek seeds (methi), and a generous sprig of curry leaves. Allow seeds to splutter without burning. Step 3 (Fry Onions & Spices): Add 1.5 cups finely sliced small shallots (sambar onions) and 4 slit green chilies. Saute on medium flame until onions turn soft and soft and pink. Step 4 (Cook on Low Heat): Add 2 chopped country tomatoes, 1.5 tbsp spicy red chili powder, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1 tbsp coriander powder, and crystal salt. Pour in the tamarind extract along with 1 cup water. Bring the gravy to a vigorous fast boil for 8-10 minutes until the raw tamarind smell disappears. Step 5 (Cook on Low Heat): Lower flame to medium. Gently slide fish slices into the boiling gravy in a single layer. Hold the pot by its handles and swirl gently to coat fish (do not stir vigorously with a ladle to avoid breaking fish). Step 6 (Finish & Serve): Cover partially and cook on low heat on low-medium heat for 12-15 minutes until fish is cooked and oil floats on the surface. Turn off heat. For authentic taste, let the curry rest for at least 3-4 hours before serving with hot rice.

ingredients: eggs, onions, tomatoes, ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder, coriander powder, turmeric, mustard seeds, cumin seeds, curry leaves, oil, salt
steps: Step 1 (Preparation): Boil 5 large eggs in salted water for 10 minutes until hard-boiled. Cool in ice water, peel shells, and make 3 vertical slits on each egg. Heat 1 tsp oil with a pinch of turmeric and chili powder in a pan; roll the boiled eggs for 2 minutes until outer skin is blistered and golden. Step 2 (Heat & Fry): Heat 2 tbsp oil in a saucepan. Add 1/2 tsp mustard seeds, 1/2 tsp cumin seeds, and 8 fresh curry leaves. Add 2 finely chopped medium onions and 2 slit green chilies; saute until golden brown. Step 3 (Fry Onions & Spices): Add 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and saute for 1 minute. Add 2 pureed ripe tomatoes, 1 tsp red chili powder, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp coriander powder, and 1/2 tsp garam masala. Cook on medium heat until oil releases from sides. Step 4 (Cook on Low Heat): Pour in 3/4 cup warm water and season with salt. Bring gravy to a gentle cook on low heat. Add the blistered boiled eggs into the gravy. Step 5 (Finish & Serve): Cover and cook on low heat on low flame for 6-8 minutes so the eggs absorb the rich masala. top with chopped cilantro and serve hot with steamed basmati rice, chapati, or parotta.

ingredients: basmati rice, chicken, onions, ginger-garlic paste, green chilies, mint leaves, coriander leaves, whole spices, ghee, oil, salt
steps: Step 1 (Prep & Wash): Wash and clean the meat/seafood thoroughly. Marinate with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, and salt for 30 minutes. Step 2 (Heat & Fry): Heat oil/ghee in a heavy pot or pressure cooker. Add whole spices, curry leaves, and sliced onions; saute until golden brown. Step 3 (Fry Onions & Spices): Add ginger-garlic paste, pureed tomatoes, red chili powder, coriander powder, and garam masala; saute until oil glistens on the edges. Step 4 (Fry Onions & Spices): Add the marinated meat and saute on medium-high heat for 6-8 minutes until seared. Step 5 (Cook on Low Heat): Add measured water, cover with lid, and cook in pressure cooker (or slow cook on low heat) until meat is fork-tender and soft and juicy. Step 6 (Cook on Low Heat): Open lid and cook on low heat for 3-5 minutes until gravy reaches desired thick, glossy thickness. Step 7 (Finish & Serve): top with fresh chopped coriander and serve hot with steamed basmati rice, Ragi Sankati, or soft rotis.

ingredients: chicken, ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, lemon juice, curry leaves, oil, salt
steps: Step 1 (Prep & Wash): Thoroughly clean and prep the meat/seafood with turmeric and lemon juice. Marinate with ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder, spices, and salt for 20 to 30 minutes in a mixing bowl. Step 2 (Heat & Fry): Heat oil/ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan or cast-iron skillet on medium flame. Add whole spices, curry leaves, and green chilies, letting them crackle vigorously. Step 3 (Fry Onions & Spices): Add finely chopped onions and saute on medium flame with a pinch of salt until caramelized and deep golden brown. Step 4 (Fry Onions & Spices): Add the marinated meat/seafood and fry on high flame for 4-5 minutes to lock in moisture and natural juices. Step 5 (Fry Onions & Spices): Lower heat to medium, cover partially, and let meat cook in its own juices until tender. Uncover and fry continuously until moisture evaporates completely. Step 6 (Step 6): Increase heat to medium-high, toss with freshly ground black pepper and roasted garam masala until crisp and dark brown. Step 7 (Finish & Serve): Turn off flame, top with freshly chopped coriander leaves, and serve hot with steamed rice, dal, or as a flavorful appetizer.

ingredients: toor dal, onions, tomatoes, ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, mustard seeds, cumin seeds, curry leaves, ghee, salt
steps: Step 1 (Prep & Wash): Rinse toor dal / moong dal thoroughly in cold water until water runs clear. Soak for 20 minutes for quick, even cooking. Step 2 (Marinate / Mix): In a pressure cooker, add soaked lentils, chopped vegetables/greens, green chilies, tomatoes, turmeric, and 2.5 cups of water. cook in pressure cooker on medium flame for 3 to 4 cooker whistles until soft and mushy. Step 3 (Step 3): Allow pressure to release naturally. Open lid, add crystal salt, and mash the dal gently using a wooden masher (pappu gutti) to a creamy thickness. Step 4 (Add Tadka (Popu)): In a small pan, heat 1.5 tbsp ghee or oil on medium flame. Add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, crushed garlic cloves, dry red chilies, and a sprig of fresh curry leaves until fragrant. Step 5 (Cook on Low Heat): Pour the sizzling tempering directly into the mashed dal. Cover immediately with a lid for 2 minutes to trap the aroma, then cook on low heat on low for 3 minutes. Step 6 (Finish & Serve): Serve piping hot poured over steamed white rice with a dollop of pure homemade ghee and spicy Andhra pickle or vadiyalu.

ingredients: toor dal, tomatoes, green chilies, onion, turmeric, ghee, mustard seeds, cumin seeds, red chilies (dried), garlic, salt, cilantro
steps: Step 1 (Prep & Wash): Rinse toor dal / moong dal thoroughly in cold water until water runs clear. Soak for 20 minutes for quick, even cooking. Step 2 (Marinate / Mix): In a pressure cooker, add soaked lentils, chopped vegetables/greens, green chilies, tomatoes, turmeric, and 2.5 cups of water. cook in pressure cooker on medium flame for 3 to 4 cooker whistles until soft and mushy. Step 3 (Step 3): Allow pressure to release naturally. Open lid, add crystal salt, and mash the dal gently using a wooden masher (pappu gutti) to a creamy thickness. Step 4 (Add Tadka (Popu)): In a small pan, heat 1.5 tbsp ghee or oil on medium flame. Add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, crushed garlic cloves, dry red chilies, and a sprig of fresh curry leaves until fragrant. Step 5 (Cook on Low Heat): Pour the sizzling tempering directly into the mashed dal. Cover immediately with a lid for 2 minutes to trap the aroma, then cook on low heat on low for 3 minutes. Step 6 (Finish & Serve): Serve piping hot poured over steamed white rice with a dollop of pure homemade ghee and spicy Andhra pickle or vadiyalu.

steps: Step 1 (Prep & Wash): Rinse toor dal / moong dal thoroughly in cold water until water runs clear. Soak for 20 minutes for quick, even cooking. ingredients: toor dal, dosakaya (yellow cucumber - peeled & cubed), tomatoes, green chilies, mustard seeds, cumin seeds, garlic, ghee, curry leaves, salt
steps: Step 1 (Prep & Wash): Rinse toor dal / moong dal thoroughly in cold water until water runs clear. Soak for 20 minutes for quick, even cooking. Step 2 (Marinate / Mix): In a pressure cooker, add soaked lentils, chopped vegetables/greens, green chilies, tomatoes, turmeric, and 2.5 cups of water. cook in pressure cooker on medium flame for 3 to 4 cooker whistles until soft and mushy. Step 3 (Step 3): Allow pressure to release naturally. Open lid, add crystal salt, and mash the dal gently using a wooden masher (pappu gutti) to a creamy thickness. Step 4 (Add Tadka (Popu)): In a small pan, heat 1.5 tbsp ghee or oil on medium flame. Add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, crushed garlic cloves, dry red chilies, and a sprig of fresh curry leaves until fragrant. Step 5 (Cook on Low Heat): Pour the sizzling tempering directly into the mashed dal. Cover immediately with a lid for 2 minutes to trap the aroma, then cook on low heat on low for 3 minutes. Step 6 (Finish & Serve): Serve piping hot poured over steamed white rice with a dollop of pure homemade ghee and spicy Andhra pickle or vadiyalu.

steps: Step 1 (Prep & Wash): Soak tamarind in warm water and extract smooth pulp. Chop tomatoes, onions, or vegetables into even cubes. Step 2 (Preparation): In a deep pot or earthen vessel, combine the tamarind extract, mashed tomatoes/vegetables, green chilies, turmeric, rasam/sambar powder, and crystal salt with 2 cups of water. Step 3 (Cook on Low Heat): Bring to a fast boil on medium heat for 10-12 minutes until the raw tamarind aroma disappears and flavors meld. Step 5 (Step 5): Pour the sizzling tempering into the hot broth. Remove from heat immediately to preserve fresh aromas, cover, and top with fresh coriander leaves. Step 6 (Finish & Serve): Serve warm as an invigorating digestive soup or mix with steaming hot rice and papad.

steps: Step 1 (Prep & Wash): Rinse toor dal / moong dal thoroughly in cold water until water runs clear. Soak for 20 minutes for quick, even cooking. ingredients: red stem gongura leaves, dried red chilies, coriander seeds, fenugreek seeds, garlic cloves, sesame oil, salt
steps: Step 1 (Preparation): Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pan; roast dals (urad/chana dal), cumin seeds, dry red chilies/green chilies, and garlic until golden and flavorful. Step 3 (Cook on Low Heat): Spread the batter thinly on a well-seasoned hot cast-iron tawa (or stream grains into boiling seasoned water for upma/pongal). Step 4 (Cook on Low Heat): Drizzle oil/ghee along edges and cook on medium flame until golden brown, crispy on the edges, and cooked through in the center. Step 5 (Step 5): Flip or fold gently when bottom turns golden and releases easily from the pan. Step 6 (Finish & Serve): Serve hot right off the stove with traditional Allam Pachadi (ginger chutney), coconut chutney, and piping hot Sambar.

ingredients: rice flour, milk (full fat), jaggery (bellam), cardamom powder, ghee, cashews, raisins
steps: Step 1 (Preparation): Heat 1-2 tbsp pure desi ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan on medium flame. Fry cashews and raisins until golden and plump; remove and set aside. Step 2 (Heat & Fry): Roast the grains/flour/semolina in ghee until flavorful and nutty, or boil milk/water in a thick pot. Step 3 (Cook on Low Heat): Cook grains/noodles in cooking on low flame milk or water on low-medium flame until thoroughly soft and tender. Step 4 (Step 4): Stir in powdered organic jaggery or sugar and continue stirring on low heat until fully dissolved and incorporated. Step 5 (Step 5): Add freshly ground cardamom powder and saffron strands soaked in warm milk; drizzle remaining ghee. Step 6 (Finish & Serve): Fold in the fried golden cashews and raisins. Serve warm or chilled as a delicious traditional dessert or festive Naivedyam.
