ingredients: rice flour, chana dal, roasted peanuts, white sesame seeds, onions, green chilies, curry leaves, ginger-garlic paste, cumin seeds, chili powder, turmeric, oil, salt
steps: Soak 3 tbsp chana dal in warm water for 30 minutes, then drain thoroughly. In a large mixing bowl, combine 2 cups rice flour, soaked chana dal, 2 tbsp crushed roasted peanuts, 1 tbsp white sesame seeds, finely chopped onion, 3 chopped green chilies, and curry leaves. Add 1 tsp cumin seeds, 1 tsp red chili powder, 1/4 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp ginger-garlic paste, and 1 tsp salt. Mix evenly with your fingers. Gradually sprinkle warm water to knead into a soft, pliable, non-sticky dough. Grease a heavy-bottomed kadai or cast-iron pan with 1 tbsp oil. Take a large ball of dough and press it evenly across the bottom and sides into a thin circular disk. Make small holes across the surface with your finger and drizzle a few drops of oil into each hole for even crisping. Cover with a lid and cook on medium-low flame for 12-15 minutes until the bottom turns golden brown and crunchy. Remove lid, cook for another 2 minutes for maximum crispiness, and serve hot with fresh butter or curd.

ingredients: basmati rice, chana dal, bottle gourd, onions, tomatoes, tamarind pulp, ginger-garlic paste, bay leaves, shahi jeera, cloves, cardamom, cinnamon, mint leaves, coriander, ghee, oil, salt
steps: Wash and soak 2 cups basmati rice for 30 minutes. In a pressure cooker, cook 1/2 cup chana dal and 1 cup diced bottle gourd with turmeric and salt for 4 whistles until tender. For the Dalcha: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pot, sauté sliced onions, ginger-garlic paste, tomatoes, red chili powder, and coriander powder. Add mashed cooked dal-gourd mix and 2 tbsp tamarind pulp. Simmer for 10 minutes until aromatic. For Bagara Rice: Heat 2 tbsp ghee in a heavy pot. Add shahi jeera, 2 bay leaves, 4 cloves, 2 cardamoms, and 1 cinnamon stick. Add thinly sliced onions and 3 slit green chilies. Fry until onions turn translucent and lightly golden. Add 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, fresh chopped mint, and coriander leaves. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Add soaked drained basmati rice and gently sauté for 1 minute to coat grains with ghee. Pour 3.5 cups boiling water and 1.5 tsp salt. Bring to a rapid boil, then reduce heat to minimum, cover tightly with a lid, and cook for 15 minutes. Turn off flame and let rest for 10 minutes. Fluff gently with a fork and serve hot Bagara Rice poured over with tangy Dalcha.

ingredients: mutton, onions, poppy seeds, coriander seeds, dry coconut, ginger-garlic paste, green chilies, curry leaves, red chili powder, garam masala, mustard oil, coriander leaves, salt
steps: Clean and wash 500g bone-in mutton. Marinate with 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tbsp red chili powder, and 1 tsp salt for 45 minutes. Dry roast 1 tbsp coriander seeds, 1 tbsp poppy seeds (khus khus), 2 tbsp grated dry coconut, and whole garam masala on low flame. Grind to a fine Telangana spice paste with little water. Heat 3 tbsp oil in a pressure cooker. Add whole spices, curry leaves, and 2 cups finely chopped onions. Sauté until onions are deep brown. Add 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and sauté until raw aroma dissipates. Add marinated mutton and sear on high flame for 8-10 minutes, stirring continuously until the meat juices evaporate and oil separates. Stir in the ground roasted Telangana spice paste, 1 tbsp spicy Guntur chili powder, and salt. Sauté for 3 minutes. Pour 1.5 cups warm water, mix well, and close pressure cooker lid. Cook for 6-7 whistles on medium flame until mutton is fall-apart tender. Release pressure naturally, simmer for 5 minutes until gravy turns thick and glossy, garnish with fresh coriander, and serve with hot rice.

ingredients: tamarind, onions, green chilies, jaggery, sesame seeds, curry leaves, mustard seeds, cumin seeds, hing, dry red chili, coriander, oil, salt
steps: Soak a lemon-sized ball of tamarind in 1.5 cups warm water for 15 minutes, squeeze thoroughly, and strain the tangy juice into a bowl. Dilute with another cup of water. Roast 4 green chilies directly over open flame or in a pan with a drop of oil until nicely charred and smoky. In a bowl or pestle, crush the roasted green chilies with 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp powdered jaggery, and 1 tbsp roasted sesame powder into a coarse paste. Add 1 cup finely chopped raw red onions and hand-crush them slightly to release their sweet pungent juices. Pour the prepared tamarind water into the onion-chili mixture and stir well to dissolve the jaggery. For tempering: Heat 1 tsp oil in a tadka pan. Add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, a pinch of hing, 1 dry red chili, and curry leaves. Let splutter. Pour hot tempering over the pulusu and mix immediately to infuse aroma. Garnish generously with finely chopped coriander leaves. Serve at room temperature alongside steamed rice and hot mudda pappu.

ingredients: mutton, onions, ginger-garlic paste, green chilies, curry leaves, coriander powder, cumin powder, red chili powder, garam masala, pepper powder, oil, salt
steps: Wash 500g tender boneless mutton pieces. Pressure cook with 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, and 1/2 cup water for 4 whistles until 80% tender. Heat 3 tbsp oil in an iron skillet or heavy bottomed pan. Add curry leaves and slit green chilies. Add finely chopped onions and fry on medium flame until golden brown and crispy. Add 1 tbsp fresh ginger-garlic paste and sauté for 2 minutes. Transfer cooked mutton along with its reduced broth into the skillet. Crank heat to high and stir fry vigorously. Add red chili powder, coriander powder, roasted cumin powder, and freshly cracked black pepper. Mix thoroughly. Continue roasting (golinchadam) on medium flame for 15-20 minutes, stirring frequently until the spices cling to the tender mutton pieces and turn dark brown. Sprinkle garam masala and fresh coriander, squeeze fresh lemon juice, and serve piping hot as a premier starter or side dish.

ingredients: raw rice, white sesame seeds, carom seeds (ajwain), oil, salt
steps: Wash and soak 3 cups raw rice for 2 hours. Drain completely and spread on a clean cotton cloth to air-dry until damp. Pound or grind the damp rice in small batches into a fine moist flour, then sift through a fine sieve. In a large bowl, mix moist rice flour, 1/2 cup white sesame seeds (til), 1 tbsp ajwain (carom seeds), and 1 tsp salt. Sprinkle warm water gradually and knead into a smooth, pliable dough that holds together without cracking. Spread a clean dry white cotton cloth on a flat table. Take small portions of dough and roll with gentle fingers into thin ropes directly on the cloth, swirling them into 3 concentric circles (sakinalu rings). Let the shaped sakinalu air-dry on the cloth for 15 minutes so they hold shape during frying. Heat oil in a deep kadai on medium heat. Lift sakinalu carefully with a flat slotted spatula and slide into hot oil. Deep-fry on medium flame until light golden and crispy, drain on paper towels.

ingredients: chicken breast, yogurt, butter, heavy cream, tomatoes, cashews, ginger-garlic paste, kashmiri chili powder, kasuri methi, garam masala, honey, oil, salt
steps: Cut 500g chicken into bite-sized cubes. Marinate with 1/2 cup yogurt, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1.5 tbsp Kashmiri chili powder, 1 tsp garam masala, 1 tbsp lemon juice, and 1 tsp salt for 1 hour. Heat 1 tbsp butter and 1 tbsp oil in a grill pan or heavy skillet. Sear marinated chicken pieces on high heat for 6-8 minutes until lightly charred and 80% cooked. Set aside. In a separate saucepan, combine 500g ripe chopped tomatoes, 15 soaked cashews, 1 sliced onion, 1 inch ginger, 4 garlic cloves, 1 bay leaf, and 1/2 cup water. Simmer covered for 15 minutes until soft. Allow the tomato-cashew mixture to cool completely, discard bay leaf, and blend in a high-speed blender into a silky smooth puree. Strain through a fine mesh sieve for classic velvety texture. Melt 3 tbsp butter in a heavy kadai. Pour in the strained velvet makhani gravy and simmer on medium flame. Stir in 1 tbsp Kashmiri chili powder for rich color, 1/2 tsp garam masala, 1 tbsp honey or sugar to balance acidity, and salt to taste. Simmer for 10 minutes until oil begins to bead on top. Add the grilled chicken pieces to the gravy and simmer gently on low flame for 6-8 minutes until chicken is tender. Finish by crushing 1 tbsp roasted kasuri methi between palms and stirring in 3 tbsp fresh heavy cream. Serve hot with garlic naan or butter roti.

ingredients: whole black urad dal, rajma (kidney beans), butter, heavy cream, tomato puree, ginger-garlic paste, kashmiri red chili, kasuri methi, garam masala, salt
steps: Wash 1 cup whole black urad dal and 1/4 cup red rajma multiple times. Soak in warm water for at least 8 hours or overnight. Drain and transfer to a pressure cooker with 4.5 cups water, 1 tsp salt, and 1 tsp Kashmiri chili powder. Pressure cook for 8-10 whistles on medium flame until completely soft and mashable. Using the back of a ladle or potato masher, gently mash a portion of the lentils against the sides of cooker to release starches and create a naturally creamy base. In a heavy bottomed pot, heat 3 tbsp butter. Add 1.5 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Add 1 cup fresh tomato puree, 1 tsp Kashmiri chili powder, and 1/2 tsp salt. Cook on medium-low flame until tomatoes reduce and butter leaves sides of pan. Pour the cooked dal into the tomato masala. Mix well and bring to a gentle boil. Add 1 cup water or milk and simmer on the lowest flame for 45 minutes to 1 hour, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking. The slow simmer is the secret to authentic creamy dhaba texture. Finish with 2 tbsp cold butter, 3 tbsp fresh cream, 1/2 tsp garam masala, and 1 tsp crushed kasuri methi. Serve hot with steamed rice or jeera rice.

ingredients: kabuli chana (chickpeas), tea bag (for dark color), all-purpose flour (maida), semolina (sooji), baking powder, yogurt, onions, tomatoes, chole masala, anardana (pomegranate seed powder), amchur, ginger juliennes, green chilies, oil, ghee, salt
steps: Soak 1.5 cups Kabuli chana overnight with 1/2 tsp baking soda. Rinse well and pressure cook with 4 cups water, 1 tea bag (tied in cheesecloth for dark color), 2 bay leaves, 1 black cardamom, and 1 tsp salt for 6 whistles until soft. For Bhature dough: Mix 2 cups maida, 2 tbsp sooji, 1/2 tsp baking powder, 1/4 tsp baking soda, 1 tsp sugar, 1/2 tsp salt, and 1/4 cup yogurt. Knead with lukewarm water into a smooth soft dough. Coat with 1 tsp oil, cover with damp cloth, and rest for 2 hours. For Chole gravy: Heat 3 tbsp ghee or oil in a deep kadai. Sauté finely minced onions until dark golden brown. Add 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and cook for 2 minutes. Stir in fresh tomato puree, 2 tbsp chole masala, 1 tsp anardana powder, 1 tsp amchur, and 1 tsp red chili powder. Cook masala until oil separates. Discard tea bag from boiled chickpeas and transfer chole along with its dark aromatic broth into the kadai. Simmer chole on medium-low flame for 15-20 minutes, lightly mashing some chickpeas with a ladle to thicken gravy. Divide rested bhatura dough into lemon-sized balls, roll on oiled board into oval discs, and deep-fry in smoking hot oil until puffed and golden on both sides. Serve steaming Amritsari chole garnished with ginger juliennes and pickled green chilies alongside hot puffy bhature.

ingredients: paneer, bell peppers, onions, hung curd, besan (gram flour), ginger-garlic paste, tomato puree, kashmiri chili powder, kasuri methi, garam masala, cream, butter, oil, salt
steps: Cut 400g paneer, 1 large bell pepper, and 1 onion into 1-inch squares. In a bowl, mix 1/2 cup hung curd, 1 tbsp roasted besan, 1 tbsp mustard oil, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tbsp Kashmiri chili powder, 1 tsp chaat masala, and salt. Coat paneer and veggies gently and marinate for 30 minutes. Pan-sear or grill marinated paneer and veggies on a hot griddle with 1 tbsp oil until golden with char marks on all sides. Set aside. For gravy: Heat 2 tbsp butter and 1 tbsp oil in a pan. Sauté finely chopped onions until golden. Add ginger-garlic paste, sauté for 1 minute, then add 1.5 cups tomato puree, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tbsp coriander powder, and 1 tsp chili powder. Cook until oil separates. Add 1/2 cup water, 1/4 cup heavy cream, 1/2 tsp garam masala, and 1 tsp crushed kasuri methi. Stir into a creamy spiced gravy. Gently fold in the grilled paneer tikka, bell peppers, and onions. Simmer for 3 minutes on low flame so flavors meld without breaking paneer. Garnish with chopped fresh coriander leaves and a swirl of cream. Serve hot with tandoori roti or naan.

recipe_name: Sarson Ka Saag & Makki Di Roti
ingredients: mustard greens (sarson), spinach (palak), bathua or methi greens, makki ka atta (maize flour), ginger, garlic, green chilies, white butter (makhan), onions, ghee, salt
steps: Wash thoroughly 500g mustard greens (sarson), 250g spinach (palak), and 150g bathua or methi. Chop roughly. Pressure cook the chopped greens with 1 inch sliced ginger, 5 garlic cloves, 3 green chilies, 1 cup water, and 1 tsp salt for 3-4 whistles until soft. Once cooled slightly, blend coarsely with a traditional wooden churner (madhani) or a pulse blender into a rustic puree (do not make baby food smooth). Transfer puree back to a pot on low heat. Dissolve 2 tbsp makki ka atta in 3 tbsp warm water and whisk into the simmering saag. Cook uncovered for 20 minutes on low flame to thicken and eliminate raw flour taste. For tempering (Tadka): Heat 2 tbsp desi ghee in a pan. Sauté 1 finely chopped onion and 1 tbsp finely minced garlic until aromatic and golden. Pour hot tadka over the bubbling saag and stir well. For Makki Roti: Knead 2 cups yellow maize flour (makki ka atta) with warm water and a pinch of salt into a soft dough. Pat between wet palms or parchment paper into round flatbreads. Cook on medium-hot tawa with ghee until speckled golden brown on both sides. Serve hot Sarson ka Saag topped with a generous dollop of homemade white butter (makhan) alongside warm Makki di Roti and jaggery (gur).

ingredients: chitra rajma (kidney beans), onions, tomatoes, ginger-garlic paste, green chilies, cumin seeds, coriander powder, kashmiri red chili, garam masala, amchur, ghee, salt
steps: Soak 1.5 cups Chitra red kidney beans in ample water overnight for at least 8 hours. Pressure cook soaked rajma with 4 cups water, 1 bay leaf, 1 black cardamom, and 1 tsp salt for 6-7 whistles until completely tender and creamy when pressed between fingers. Heat 2 tbsp ghee or oil in a deep pan. Add 1 tsp cumin seeds and let crackle. Add 2 cups finely grated onions and sauté on medium heat until golden brown. Add 1.5 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and 2 slit green chilies. Cook for 2 minutes until raw aroma is gone. Stir in 1.5 cups fresh tomato puree, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tbsp coriander powder, 1 tsp Kashmiri red chili powder, and 1/2 tsp salt. Cook until oil separates from the masala. Add the cooked rajma along with its cooking water. Stir and mash a ladleful of kidney beans against the pan wall to create a thick luscious gravy. Simmer gently on low flame for 15-20 minutes. Finish with 1/2 tsp garam masala, 1/2 tsp amchur powder, and chopped coriander leaves. Serve hot with steaming jeera rice.

ingredients: besan (gram flour), sooji (semolina), eno fruit salt, citric acid or lemon juice, ginger-green chili paste, turmeric, sugar, mustard seeds, sesame seeds, curry leaves, green chilies, coriander, oil, salt
steps: In a bowl, whisk 1.5 cups sifted besan, 1 tbsp fine semolina (sooji), 1/4 tsp turmeric, 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tsp lemon juice, 1 tsp ginger-green chili paste, 1 tsp salt, and 1 tbsp oil. Gradually add 1 cup water and whisk vigorously in one direction for 3 minutes to incorporate air into a smooth, lump-free pouring batter. Grease a cake tin or steaming plate with oil. Boil water in a steamer or large kadai with a stand. Right before steaming, add 1 tsp Eno fruit salt (or baking soda + citric acid) to the batter with 1 tsp water over it. Whisk gently until the batter turns light, foamy, and doubles in volume. Immediately pour batter into the greased tin. Place in the steamer, cover tightly with lid, and steam on high flame for 15-18 minutes. Check with a toothpick; it should come out clean. Turn off flame and let cool for 5 minutes, then invert onto a plate and slice into squares. For tempering (Tadka): Heat 1 tbsp oil in a small pan. Add mustard seeds, sesame seeds, pinch of hing, 4 slit green chilies, and curry leaves. Sauté for 30 seconds. Add 1/2 cup water and 1 tbsp sugar. Bring to a boil. Slowly ladle the sweet tangy warm tempering water evenly all over the sliced dhokla squares so they soak it up and become melt-in-mouth juicy. Garnish with coriander and fresh coconut.

ingredients: whole wheat flour, fresh fenugreek leaves (methi), besan, yogurt, ginger-garlic-chili paste, sesame seeds, carom seeds (ajwain), turmeric, red chili powder, coriander powder, oil, salt
steps: Wash 1.5 cups fresh fenugreek leaves thoroughly, drain water completely, and finely chop. In a large mixing bowl, combine 2 cups whole wheat flour, 2 tbsp besan (adds softness), chopped methi leaves, 1 tbsp white sesame seeds, and 1/2 tsp ajwain (rubbed between palms). Add 1 tsp ginger-garlic-chili paste, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp chili powder, 1 tsp coriander powder, 1 tsp salt, 2 tbsp oil, and 3 tbsp thick yogurt (keeps theplas soft for days). Mix well, then add water in small increments to knead into a soft, smooth dough. Coat with 1/2 tsp oil and rest for 10 minutes. Divide dough into small balls. Dust with flour and roll out as thin as possible on a flat board into round discs. Heat a tawa on medium-high flame. Place thepla on tawa and cook until small bubbles appear on surface. Flip, brush with a little oil, and gently press with a spatula. Flip again, apply oil on other side, and cook until light golden brown spots appear. Stack warm theplas together to keep them ultra-soft. Serve warm with mango chunda, lemon pickle, or masala chai.

ingredients: surti papdi (flat beans), tuvar lilva (fresh pigeon peas), baby potatoes, purple yam (kand), sweet potato, baby brinjals, fresh methi leaves, besan, fresh grated coconut, coriander, green garlic, ginger-green chili paste, sesame seeds, ajwain, jaggery, oil, salt
steps: Prepare Methi Muthias: Mix 1 cup chopped methi, 1/2 cup besan, 2 tbsp sooji, pinch of turmeric, chili powder, sugar, salt, and 1 tbsp oil. Knead into firm dough, shape into small cylindrical dumplings, and deep fry or steam until golden. Prepare Masala: Grind 1/2 cup grated fresh coconut, 1/2 cup chopped coriander, 1/4 cup green garlic, 2 tbsp sesame seeds, 1.5 tbsp ginger-chili paste, 1 tbsp coriander-cumin powder, 1 tbsp powdered jaggery, and salt into a coarse aromatic green paste. Slit baby brinjals and baby potatoes criss-cross without cutting all the way through, and stuff them with half of the prepared green coconut masala. String and shell Surti papdi and fresh tuvar beans. Peel and dice kand (purple yam) and sweet potato into cubes. Heat 4 tbsp oil in a heavy-bottomed pot or pressure cooker. Add 1 tsp ajwain and a pinch of hing. Add the surti papdi, tuvar lilva, diced yam, and sweet potatoes. Sauté for 3 minutes. Add the remaining green coconut masala and toss gently. Layer the stuffed brinjals, potatoes, and fried methi muthias carefully on top. Pour 1/2 cup warm water around the edges. Cover tightly and slow cook on minimum flame for 30 minutes (or pressure cook on low for 1 whistle) without stirring so vegetables cook in their steam. Garnish with green garlic and serve with hot puris.

ingredients: toor dal (pigeon peas), peanuts, tomatoes, jaggery (gud), kokum or lemon juice, ginger-green chili paste, mustard seeds, cumin seeds, fenugreek seeds (methi), cinnamon stick, cloves, curry leaves, ghee, salt
steps: Wash 1 cup toor dal and pressure cook with 3 cups water, 2 tbsp raw peanuts, 1/2 tsp turmeric, and salt for 4 whistles until completely mushy. Whisk the cooked dal with an immersion blender or wooden churner into a silky smooth liquid consistency. Add 1.5 cups water if needed. Transfer dal to a pot. Add 1 chopped tomato, 1 tbsp ginger-green chili paste, 2 soaked kokum petals (or 1.5 tbsp lemon juice), and 2 tbsp crumbled jaggery for that signature sweet-tangy balance. Bring the dal to a gentle boil on medium heat and simmer for 10 minutes so peanuts and jaggery absorb spices. In a tadka pan, heat 1.5 tbsp ghee. Add 1/2 tsp mustard seeds, 1/2 tsp cumin seeds, and 1/4 tsp methi seeds. Add 1 cinnamon stick, 3 cloves, 1 dry red chili, pinch of hing, and fresh curry leaves. Allow to crackle. Pour hot fragrant ghee tadka directly into the simmering dal and cover with lid for 2 minutes to trap aromas. Stir well, garnish with fresh chopped coriander leaves, and serve warm with steamed basmati rice or rotli.

ingredients: rice, chana dal, toor dal, urad dal, grated bottle gourd (lauki), yogurt, ginger-green chili paste, mustard seeds, sesame seeds, curry leaves, ajwain, turmeric, baking soda, oil, salt
steps: Combine 1 cup rice, 1/2 cup chana dal, 1/4 cup toor dal, and 2 tbsp urad dal. Wash and soak in warm water for 4-5 hours. Drain and grind the lentils with 1/2 cup sour yogurt into a coarse, thick batter (like idli batter). Ferment overnight for 8 hours in a warm place. To the fermented batter, add 1 cup peeled and grated bottle gourd (lauki), 1 tbsp ginger-green chili paste, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp chili powder, 1 tsp sugar, and 1 tsp salt. Mix well, then stir in 1/2 tsp baking soda or fruit salt with 1 tbsp oil to make it airy. Heat 2 tbsp oil in a heavy non-stick pan or traditional handvo cooker on low flame. Add 1 tsp mustard seeds, 1.5 tbsp white sesame seeds, 1/2 tsp ajwain, and curry leaves. Let crackle. Pour 2 cups of the handvo batter into the pan, spreading evenly into a 1-inch thick cake. Sprinkle more sesame seeds on top. Cover tightly with a lid and cook on low heat for 15-18 minutes until the bottom crust is deeply golden brown and crisp. Carefully flip the handvo cake using a plate, add 1 tsp oil around edges, and cook uncovered for another 10-12 minutes until both sides are crunchy and center is set. Slice into wedges and serve with green chutney.

ingredients: ratlami sev or thick besan sev, ripe juicy tomatoes, ginger, garlic, green chilies, mustard seeds, cumin seeds, hing, kashmiri red chili powder, coriander-cumin powder, jaggery, oil, coriander, salt
steps: Dice 4 large ripe red juicy tomatoes into medium cubes. Heat 2 tbsp oil in a pan on medium flame. Add 1/2 tsp mustard seeds, 1/2 tsp cumin seeds, and a generous pinch of hing (asafoetida). Add 1 tbsp finely minced garlic, 1 tsp grated ginger, and 2 chopped green chilies. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Add the chopped tomatoes, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1.5 tsp Kashmiri chili powder (for bright red Kathiyawadi color), 1 tbsp coriander-cumin powder, and 1 tsp salt. Sauté on medium flame for 4 minutes until tomatoes soften slightly but retain chunks. Add 3/4 cup warm water and 1 tbsp crumbled jaggery to balance the natural tanginess of tomatoes. Simmer for 3 minutes into a rich saucy gravy. Just before serving, stir in 1 cup of thick crispy gram flour sev (Ratlami or Gujarati Gathiya sev) and turn off flame immediately so sev absorbs gravy while keeping some texture. Garnish with lots of fresh chopped coriander leaves and serve immediately with hot phulkas, parathas, or bajra rotla.

ingredients: rohu or katla fish steaks, yellow mustard seeds, black mustard seeds, poppy seeds (posto), green chilies, mustard oil, turmeric, kalonji (nigella seeds), salt
steps: Wash 4 thick cut Rohu or Katla fish steaks. Marinate with 1 tsp turmeric powder and 1 tsp salt for 15 minutes. Soak 2 tbsp yellow mustard seeds, 1 tbsp black mustard seeds, and 1 tbsp poppy seeds in warm water for 20 minutes. Grind the soaked seeds with 2 green chilies, a pinch of salt, and 1/4 cup water into an ultra-smooth paste (salt prevents the mustard from turning bitter). Strain the mustard paste through a sieve with 1/2 cup water to remove black seed hulls for a smooth digestible gravy. Heat 3 tbsp pure mustard oil in a kadai until smoking hot, then reduce heat. Lightly fry marinated fish steaks for 1.5 minutes per side until light golden. Do not overfry. Remove fish. In the same fragrant oil, add 1/2 tsp kalonji (nigella seeds) and 3 slit green chilies. Let them sizzle. Pour in the strained mustard paste, 1/2 tsp turmeric, and salt. Bring to a gentle boil. Slide in the fried fish steaks, cover, and simmer on medium-low flame for 6-8 minutes. Drizzle 1 tsp raw mustard oil on top for sharp punch and serve with steaming hot Gobindobhog rice.

ingredients: goat mutton, yogurt, onions, potatoes, ginger-garlic paste, mustard oil, kashmiri red chili powder, turmeric, whole garam masala (cardamom, cinnamon, cloves), sugar, ghee, salt
steps: Wash 600g tender goat meat. Marinate with 1/2 cup beaten yogurt, 2 tbsp mustard oil, 1.5 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tbsp Kashmiri chili powder, and 1 tsp salt for 2 hours. Peel 2 large potatoes, cut into halves, rub with pinch of turmeric and salt, and shallow fry in mustard oil until golden brown. Set aside. Heat 4 tbsp mustard oil in a heavy iron kadai or Dutch oven. Add 1 tsp sugar and let it caramelize to deep red (this gives Kosha Mangsho its iconic dark mahogany hue). Add whole garam masala (2 bay leaves, 4 green cardamoms, 1 cinnamon stick, 4 cloves). Add 2.5 cups finely sliced onions and fry on medium flame for 12-15 minutes until deep brown. Add 1.5 tbsp ginger paste, 1.5 tbsp garlic paste, and 1 tbsp chili powder. Sauté with splashes of water until oil floats on top. Add marinated mutton to the kadai. Sauté vigorously on medium-high heat (koshano) for 25-30 minutes, turning constantly as the meat sears and absorbs the spices. Once meat turns deep brown and oil separates, add the fried potato halves and 1.5 cups hot water. Cover tightly and simmer on low heat for 45 minutes (or transfer to pressure cooker for 5 whistles) until melt-in-mouth tender. Finish with 1 tsp Bengali garam masala and 1 tbsp desi ghee. Serve thick rich Kosha Mangsho with hot puffed Luchis or Basanti Pulao.

ingredients: chana dal (bengal gram), fresh coconut slices, raisins, ginger paste, bay leaf, cinnamon, cardamom, cumin seeds, hing, sugar, ghee, maida (for luchi), oil, salt
steps: Wash and soak 1.5 cups chana dal for 1 hour. Pressure cook with 3 cups water, 1/2 tsp turmeric, and 1 tsp salt for 3 whistles until cooked yet holding firm grain shape. In a kadai, heat 2 tbsp ghee. Fry 1/4 cup thinly sliced fresh coconut bits until golden brown and crispy. Drain and set aside. In the same aromatic ghee, add 1 bay leaf, 3 green cardamoms, 1 cinnamon stick, 1/2 tsp cumin seeds, and a pinch of hing. Let crackle. Add 1.5 tbsp ginger paste, 1 tsp cumin powder, 1/2 tsp turmeric, and 1/2 tsp red chili powder mixed with 2 tbsp water. Sauté until ghee separates. Pour cooked chana dal into the masala. Add 1.5 tbsp sugar (authentic Bengali Chholar Dal is distinctly sweet and savory) and raisins. Simmer for 8-10 minutes on medium heat until gravy thickens slightly. Stir in the fried coconut bits, 1/2 tsp Bengali garam masala powder, and 1 tsp melted ghee. For Luchis: Knead maida with oil, pinch of salt, and water into soft dough. Roll into thin discs and deep fry in hot oil until puffed white like balloons. Serve hot with Chholar Dal.

recipe_name: Aloo Posto (Potatoes in Poppy Seed Paste)
ingredients: potatoes, posto (white poppy seeds), green chilies, kalonji (nigella seeds), turmeric, mustard oil, salt
steps: Peel 4 medium potatoes and cut into uniform 1/2 inch cubes. Soak in cold water for 10 minutes to remove excess starch. Soak 4 tbsp white poppy seeds (posto) in 1/4 cup warm water for 20 minutes. Grind the soaked poppy seeds with 3 green chilies and 2-3 tbsp water in a stone sil-batta or spice blender into a thick, creamy, grainy white paste. Heat 2.5 tbsp pure mustard oil in a kadai until smoking, then lower flame. Add 1/2 tsp kalonji (nigella seeds) and 2 slit green chilies. Let them sizzle and fragrance the oil. Add the potato cubes and sauté on medium flame for 5 minutes with 1/4 tsp turmeric and 1 tsp salt until lightly browned. Pour 1/2 cup hot water, cover with lid, and cook on low heat for 8-10 minutes until potatoes are fork-tender. Add the creamy posto paste and 1/2 tsp sugar. Mix gently, cook uncovered for 2-3 minutes until the thick paste clings lusciously to every potato cube, drizzle with 1 tsp raw mustard oil, and serve with Biulir Dal and rice.

recipe_name: Chingri Malai Curry (Prawns in Coconut Milk)
ingredients: tiger prawns or jumbo shrimp, thick coconut milk, thin coconut milk, onions, ginger paste, garlic paste, green chilies, cinnamon, green cardamom, cloves, turmeric, kashmiri red chili, mustard oil, ghee, sugar, salt
steps: Clean and devein 500g large prawns, leaving the head and tail intact for flavor. Rub with 1/2 tsp turmeric and 1/2 tsp salt. Heat 2 tbsp mustard oil in a pan. Lightly sear the prawns on medium heat for exactly 1 minute per side until they turn pink. Remove immediately to prevent rubberiness. In the same oil, add 1 tbsp ghee, 2 bay leaves, 3 cracked green cardamoms, 1-inch cinnamon, and 3 cloves. Add 1 cup finely pureed onions and sauté on medium heat until golden and sweet. Add 1 tbsp ginger paste, 1 tsp garlic paste, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp Kashmiri chili powder, and 1 tsp salt. Cook until oil separates. Pour 1 cup thin coconut milk and simmer for 5 minutes until gravy becomes cohesive and thickens. Gently slide in the seared prawns and 4 slit green chilies. Pour 1/2 cup rich thick coconut cream and 1 tsp sugar to highlight coconut sweetness. Simmer covered on low heat for 4-5 minutes until prawns are tender and infused with gravy. Serve with fragrant Basmati rice.

ingredients: chicken leg quarters, yogurt, cashew paste, char magaz (melon seed) paste, poppy seed paste, ginger-garlic paste, onion paste, sattoo (roasted gram flour), rose water, meetha ittar (edible perfume), ghee, kashmiri chili powder, mace and nutmeg powder, salt
steps: Flatten and score 4 whole chicken leg quarters with deep cuts so marinade penetrates the bone. Prepare Royal Marinade: Whisk 1 cup thick hung curd, 2 tbsp cashew-poppy-melon seed paste, 2 tbsp fried onion paste, 1.5 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tbsp roasted gram flour (sattoo), 1.5 tbsp Kashmiri chili, 1/2 tsp mace-nutmeg (jaiphal-javitri) powder, 1/2 tsp white pepper, 1 tsp rose water, 2 drops meetha ittar, and 1.5 tsp salt. Coat chicken thoroughly in marinade and refrigerate for at least 4 hours (overnight recommended). Heat 4 tbsp ghee in a wide, heavy-bottomed flat pan or lagan. Place chicken pieces in a single layer without overcrowding. Fry on medium flame for 8-10 minutes, basting occasionally with remaining marinade. Turn chicken pieces over carefully to develop a golden crust. Pour the rest of the rich marinade over the chicken, cover with a tight lid, and simmer on lowest flame (Dum style) for 30 minutes until chicken is super tender and ghee floats on top. Serve hot chicken chaap with Kolkata Biryani or Roomali Roti.

ingredients: potatoes, cauliflower, green peas, bell peppers, onions, tomatoes, pav bhaji masala, kashmiri red chili paste, ginger-garlic paste, butter, lemon, coriander, pav bread, salt
steps: Boil 3 large potatoes, 1 cup cauliflower florets, and 1/2 cup green peas until completely soft. Drain and mash roughly. Heat 2 tbsp butter and 1 tbsp oil on a large flat tawa or skillet. Add 1 cup finely chopped onions and sauté until translucent. Add 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and 1/2 cup finely chopped green bell peppers (capsicum). Sauté for 3 minutes until peppers are soft. Add 1.5 cups finely chopped ripe tomatoes, 2 tbsp Kashmiri red chili paste, 2 tbsp authentic Pav Bhaji masala, and 1 tsp salt. Cook until tomatoes breakdown and butter oozes out. Add the boiled mashed vegetables and 1 cup warm water. Using a traditional potato masher, mash everything vigorously directly on the tawa until velvety smooth. Simmer for 10-12 minutes on medium-low flame, adding water to achieve luscious spreadable consistency. Stir in 2 tbsp extra salted butter, a squeeze of fresh lemon juice, and finely chopped fresh coriander. Slice pav buns horizontally, toast on the buttered tawa sprinkled with a pinch of pav bhaji masala and coriander, and serve hot with bhaji, onion rings, and lemon wedges.

ingredients: sprouted matki (moth beans), farsan / mixed sev, onions, tomatoes, dry coconut, ginger-garlic paste, kolhapuri kanda lasun masala, mustard seeds, hing, curry leaves, oil, pav bread, lemon, salt
steps: Boil 2 cups sprouted matki (moth beans) with 1/2 tsp turmeric and salt for 8 minutes until tender but not mushy. For Kolhapuri Vatan (Masala): Roast 1 sliced onion and 1/2 cup grated dry coconut in 1 tsp oil until deep brown. Grind with ginger, garlic, and fresh coriander into a fine paste. Heat 3 tbsp oil in a deep kadai. Add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, pinch of hing, and curry leaves. Let crackle. Add the roasted coconut-onion vatan and sauté on medium heat until fragrant and oil separates. Add 2 tbsp spicy Kolhapuri Kanda Lasun Masala, 1 tsp Kashmiri chili powder, and 1 tsp coriander powder. Sauté for 1 minute. Add boiled sprouted matki and 3 cups water. Bring to a rapid rolling boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes until a fiery red oil layer ('Kat' or 'Tarri') forms on top. To Assemble: In a serving bowl, add 2 ladles of boiled matki beans, top generously with crispy mixed farsan, finely chopped onions, and fresh coriander. Ladle piping hot fiery Kolhapuri red Kat (tarri gravy) all over the farsan. Serve immediately with warm buttered pav and lemon wedges.

ingredients: chana dal (bengal gram), jaggery (gul), cardamom powder, nutmeg powder (jaiphal), whole wheat flour, maida, turmeric, ghee, salt
steps: Cook 1 cup chana dal with 2.5 cups water and a drop of oil in a pressure cooker for 4 whistles until completely soft. Drain the excess dal water (reserve it for making spicy Katachi Amti). In a heavy pan, combine hot cooked chana dal and 1 cup powdered jaggery. Cook on medium-low heat, mashing constantly as jaggery melts and thickens into a dense sweet paste (puran). Test puran consistency: insert a spoon upright; if it stands without falling, puran is ready. Stir in 1 tsp cardamom powder and 1/4 tsp freshly grated nutmeg. Pass hot puran through a traditional puran yantra or fine sieve to get a lump-free silky filling. Let cool and shape into tennis-ball sized portions. Knead 1 cup wheat flour, 1/2 cup maida, pinch of turmeric, 2 tbsp oil, and water into an ultra-soft, stretchy dough (poli dough). Rest for 30 minutes. Flatten a ball of dough, place a slightly larger ball of puran filling inside, bring edges together and seal tightly. Dust with rice flour and roll out gently into a thin, even circular flatbread. Cook on hot tawa on medium flame until puffed like a balloon with golden spots. Smear generously with melted desi ghee and serve warm.

ingredients: thick poha (flattened rice), onions, potatoes (optional), raw peanuts, mustard seeds, green chilies, curry leaves, turmeric, sugar, fresh lemon juice, fresh grated coconut, coriander, oil, salt
steps: Place 2.5 cups thick poha in a colander. Rinse gently under running water for 30 seconds until moistened. Drain all water thoroughly, sprinkle 1/2 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp sugar, toss gently, and rest for 10 minutes to fluff. Heat 2 tbsp oil in a kadai on medium heat. Add 1/4 cup raw peanuts and fry until golden and crunchy. Remove half the peanuts for garnish. In the same oil, add 1 tsp mustard seeds, 1/4 tsp hing, 3 slit green chilies, and 10 fresh curry leaves. Let crackle. Add 1.5 cups finely chopped onions (kanda) and sauté on medium heat until soft and translucent (do not brown). Add 1/2 tsp turmeric powder and mix into the fragrant onions. Gently fold in the softened fluffy poha. Toss gently using a flat spatula so flattened rice grains stay whole and turn sunny yellow. Cover with a lid and steam on the lowest heat for 3-4 minutes so poha absorbs moisture and flavors. Turn off flame, squeeze juice of 1 fresh lemon, toss, and garnish generously with chopped coriander leaves, fresh grated coconut, and crunchy peanuts.

ingredients: chicken, dry coconut, onions, ginger-garlic paste, kolhapuri kanda lasun masala, coriander seeds, cumin seeds, curry leaves, oil, coriander, lemon, salt
steps: Marinate 500g bone-in chicken with 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, and 1 tsp salt for 30 minutes. Dry roast 1/2 cup grated dry coconut, 1 sliced onion, 1 tbsp coriander seeds, 1 tsp cumin seeds, 3 cloves, and 1 cinnamon stick on low flame until deep golden. Grind with little water into a coarse roasted Sukka masala. Heat 3 tbsp oil in a heavy kadai. Add curry leaves and 1 finely chopped onion. Sauté until golden brown. Add 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute. Add marinated chicken and sear on high heat for 6-8 minutes until meat changes color and releases juices. Cover and cook chicken in its own juices on medium heat for 12 minutes until 80% cooked. Uncover, add the ground roasted coconut Sukka masala and 2 tbsp Kolhapuri Kanda Lasun Masala. Toss vigorously on high heat. Continue pan-roasting on medium flame for 10-12 minutes until all gravy evaporates and the spiced coconut masala coats every chicken piece in a dry savory crust. Garnish with coriander and lemon.

ingredients: sabudana (tapioca pearls), roasted peanuts, potatoes, green chilies, cumin seeds, ghee, sugar, lemon juice, rock salt (sendha namak) or salt, coriander
steps: Wash 1.5 cups sabudana in cold water 3-4 times to rinse off surface starch. Drain completely, add 1 cup water (just enough to touch pearls), cover, and soak overnight for 6-8 hours until pearls are soft and crush easily. Dry roast 3/4 cup peanuts on medium heat, let cool, remove skins, and pulse into a coarse powder (danyacha koot). Gently mix the coarse peanut powder, 1 tsp sugar, and 1 tsp salt directly into the soaked sabudana pearls (this prevents pearls from clumping during cooking). Heat 2 tbsp ghee or peanut oil in a non-stick pan. Add 1 tsp cumin seeds and let crackle. Add 1 small potato diced into tiny cubes and fry on medium-low heat until golden and tender. Add 3 finely chopped green chilies and sauté for 30 seconds. Add the peanut-coated sabudana to the pan. Toss gently on medium-low flame for 3-4 minutes. Cover with a lid and cook on lowest flame for 2-3 minutes until tapioca pearls turn translucent. Remove lid, squeeze fresh lemon juice, toss with fresh coriander, and serve hot.

ingredients: raw rice, cooked rice, grated coconut, yeast or toddy, thick coconut milk, thin coconut milk, potatoes, carrots, beans, ginger, green chilies, curry leaves, cinnamon, cardamom, coconut oil, salt
steps: Soak 2 cups raw rice for 4 hours. Grind with 1 cup grated coconut, 1/2 cup cooked rice, 1/2 tsp yeast, 2 tbsp sugar, and water into a smooth silky batter. Ferment for 8 hours until foamy and light. For Vegetable Stew: Heat 1.5 tbsp coconut oil in a pan. Add 1 cinnamon stick, 3 cardamoms, 3 cloves, sliced ginger, slit green chilies, and curry leaves. Add 1 sliced onion and sauté until translucent (do not brown). Add diced potatoes, carrots, and green beans. Pour 1.5 cups thin coconut milk and 1 tsp salt. Simmer covered for 12-15 minutes until vegetables are tender. Pour 1/2 cup thick coconut milk, gently warm through without boiling, drizzle 1 tsp raw coconut oil and curry leaves on top, and remove from heat. For Appam: Heat an appachatti (curved appam pan). Pour a ladle of batter into the center. Holding both handles of the pan, swirl quickly in a circular motion so batter coats sides into a thin lace and collects thick in the center. Cover with lid and cook on medium-low flame for 2-3 minutes until edges turn crisp and golden and center is fluffy and soft. Serve warm with coconut vegetable stew.

ingredients: seer fish (kingfish) or pomfret, kudampuli (malabar tamarind), shallots (cheriya ulli), ginger, garlic, green chilies, curry leaves, kashmiri chili powder, fenugreek powder, coconut oil, salt
steps: Clean and cut 500g kingfish or pomfret into steaks. Wash 3 pieces of Kudampuli (Malabar tamarind) and soak in 1/2 cup warm water. In an authentic clay pot (Meen Chatti) or heavy pan, heat 3 tbsp coconut oil on medium heat. Add 1/2 tsp mustard seeds and 1/4 tsp fenugreek seeds (methi). Let crackle. Add 1 cup sliced shallots, 1 tbsp julienned ginger, 1 tbsp sliced garlic, 3 slit green chilies, and 2 sprigs of curry leaves. Sauté until shallots turn soft and light golden. Make a paste of 2 tbsp Kashmiri red chili powder, 1/2 tsp turmeric, and 1 tbsp coriander powder with 3 tbsp water. Add to the pot and sauté on low flame until oil separates. Pour in the soaked Kudampuli along with its tangy water and 1.5 cups additional water with 1 tsp salt. Bring to a rolling boil. Slide the fish steaks into the boiling gravy in a single layer. Swirl the pot gently by hand (do not use spoon as fish can break). Cover and simmer on medium-low heat for 15-18 minutes until fish is cooked and gravy turns deep crimson and thick. Rest for at least 2 hours before serving for incredible depth of flavor with Kerala matta rice.

ingredients: jeerakasala (kaima) rice, chicken, onions, tomatoes, green chili-ginger-garlic paste, yogurt, malabar garam masala, turmeric, mint leaves, coriander leaves, cashews, raisins, ghee, salt
steps: Wash 2 cups aromatic short-grain Kaima (Jeerakasala) rice and soak for 20 minutes. Heat 2 tbsp ghee in a pot, fry cashews and raisins until golden and set aside. In the same ghee, fry sliced onions until deep golden (Bista) for garnish. In the same pot, fry drained kaima rice for 2 minutes. Pour 4 cups boiling water, 1 tsp salt, and 1 tsp lemon juice. Cook covered on low heat until water is absorbed and rice is fluffy. Keep aside. For Chicken Masala: Heat 3 tbsp ghee in a heavy biryani pot. Sauté 3 cups sliced onions until soft. Add 2.5 tbsp crushed green chili-ginger-garlic paste and sauté for 3 minutes until raw smell goes. Add chopped tomatoes, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1.5 tbsp Malabar garam masala, 3 tbsp yogurt, and 1 tsp salt. Cook until tomatoes are mushy. Add 600g chicken pieces, fresh mint, and coriander. Cook covered on medium heat without adding water for 20-25 minutes until chicken is tender and coated in thick masala. Layering: Level the chicken masala at the bottom of the pot. Layer the cooked fragrant Kaima rice evenly over the chicken. Top with fried golden onions, cashews, raisins, mint, coriander, and 1 tbsp melted ghee. Seal with foil and lid, place on a hot tawa on low heat for 15 minutes Dum, and serve with date pickle and coconut raita.

ingredients: puttu podi (coarse rice flour), fresh grated coconut, kala chana (black chickpeas), onions, tomatoes, coconut slices, ginger-garlic paste, coriander powder, kashmiri chili powder, garam masala, curry leaves, mustard seeds, coconut oil, salt
steps: Soak 1 cup black chickpeas (kadala) overnight. Pressure cook with 3 cups water and 1 tsp salt for 6 whistles until soft. For Kadala Curry: Dry roast 1/2 cup grated coconut with 1 tbsp coriander powder, 1 tbsp chili powder, and fennel seeds until deep brown. Grind into a smooth roasted coconut paste. Heat 2 tbsp coconut oil in a pan. Sauté mustard seeds, curry leaves, thinly sliced coconut bites, onions, and ginger-garlic paste until brown. Add chopped tomatoes, boiled black chickpeas, roasted coconut paste, and 1 cup water. Simmer for 15 minutes until gravy turns dark and aromatic. For Puttu: Take 2 cups roasted puttu flour (rice flour) in a bowl with 1/2 tsp salt. Sprinkle lukewarm water in small sprinkles, gently rubbing with fingers until flour resembles wet breadcrumbs that hold shape when squeezed but crumble easily. In a cylindrical puttu maker (Puttukutti), add 2 tbsp grated fresh coconut at the bottom, then fill with 3 inches of prepared moist puttu flour, followed by another layer of coconut. Attach the cylinder to the boiling puttu pot or pressure cooker nozzle. Steam on high flame for 5-6 minutes until steam jets steadily out of the top vents. Gently push the steamed cylindrical puttu out onto a plate using a wooden rod and serve steaming hot with spicy Kadala curry and ripe bananas.

ingredients: raw plantain (nendran), elephant yam (chena), drumstick (muringakka), carrots, snake gourd (padavalanga), ash gourd (kumbalanga), green chilies, grated coconut, cumin seeds, sour curd (yogurt), turmeric, coconut oil, curry leaves, salt
steps: Cut all mixed vegetables (raw plantain, yam, drumstick, carrot, snake gourd, ash gourd) into uniform 2-inch long thin batons. In a heavy cooking pot, add the firm vegetables first (yam, plantain, drumstick) with 1/2 cup water, 1/2 tsp turmeric, and 1 tsp salt. Cover and cook for 5 minutes. Add the softer vegetables (carrot, gourds) on top, cover, and steam on low flame for 8-10 minutes until all vegetables are cooked tender but hold their crisp shape. For coconut paste: Coarsely grind 1.5 cups fresh grated coconut, 4 green chilies, and 1 tsp cumin seeds using pulse mode (do not make a fine paste; it should remain rough and coarse). Add the coarse coconut mixture to the cooked vegetables and gently toss without breaking the vegetable sticks. Simmer on low heat for 3 minutes until raw flavor subsides. Remove pot from flame and stir in 1/3 cup whisked sour curd (or raw mango slices) to give signature tanginess. Drizzle 2 tbsp pure virgin coconut oil all over the hot avial and scatter fresh curry leaves. Cover pot immediately and let rest for 10 minutes before serving on Sadya leaf.

ingredients: whole pearl spot fish (karimeen) or pomfret, banana leaves, shallots, tomatoes, ginger, garlic, green chilies, curry leaves, kashmiri chili powder, turmeric, black pepper, coconut oil, lemon juice, salt
steps: Clean 2 whole Karimeen (pearl spot fish) and score deeply on both sides. Marinate with 1 tsp chili powder, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1/2 tsp pepper, 1 tbsp lemon juice, and 1 tsp salt for 20 minutes. Shallow fry fish in 2 tbsp coconut oil for 2 minutes per side until 60% cooked. Set aside. In the same pan, add 1.5 cups finely sliced shallots, 1 tbsp minced ginger, 1 tbsp minced garlic, 3 slit green chilies, and curry leaves. Sauté until shallots turn soft brown. Add 1 finely chopped tomato, 1 tbsp Kashmiri chili powder, 1/2 tsp turmeric, and salt. Cook until tomatoes breakdown into a thick spicy onion-tomato masala. Gently pass fresh banana leaves over open flame for 5 seconds to wilt them so they become pliable without tearing. Place a wilted banana leaf on a board. Spread a generous layer of onion-tomato masala, place the fried fish on top, and cover with more masala on top. Wrap the banana leaf tightly into a rectangular packet and tie with banana fiber or kitchen twine. Heat 1 tbsp coconut oil in a cast iron tawa. Place the banana leaf parcels, cover with lid, and slow-roast on low-medium flame for 8-10 minutes on each side until the leaf chars and infuses fish with smoky aroma. Unwrap and serve hot.

ingredients: sona masoori rice, toor dal, shallots (sambar onions), carrots, beans, peas, tamarind pulp, jaggery, bisi bele bath powder (with kapok buds/marathi moggu), mustard seeds, dry red chilies, curry leaves, cashews, ghee, salt
steps: Wash 1 cup rice and 3/4 cup toor dal together. Pressure cook with 4 cups water, 1/2 tsp turmeric, and 1 tsp oil for 4-5 whistles until very soft and mashable. In a separate pot, boil 1 cup mixed vegetables (carrots, beans, peas, peeled shallots) with 1 cup water and salt until tender. Soak a lemon-sized tamarind ball in warm water and extract 1/2 cup thick pulp. In a large heavy pot, combine the boiled vegetables, tamarind extract, 1 tbsp powdered jaggery, 2.5 tbsp authentic Bisi Bele Bath powder (spiced with marathi moggu, cinnamon, and coconut), and 1/2 cup water. Boil for 6-8 minutes until raw tamarind taste disappears. Add the cooked soft rice and dal mash to the boiling vegetable-spice mixture. Stir well with a ladle, mashing slightly. Add 1 cup hot water to adjust to a semi-liquid, porridge-like consistency (it thickens substantially as it cools). Simmer on low heat for 5 minutes. For Tempering: Heat 3 tbsp ghee in a tadka pan. Add mustard seeds, 2 dry red chilies, curry leaves, pinch of hing, and 12 cashews. Fry until cashews turn golden brown. Pour hot fragrant ghee tadka over the bubbling Bisi Bele Bath. Mix well, let rest for 5 minutes, and serve hot topped with potato chips or boondi.

ingredients: dosa batter (rice, urad dal, chana dal, poha), potatoes, onions, green chilies, ginger, red garlic chutney (byadgi chilies, garlic, roasted chana), butter, mustard seeds, curry leaves, salt
steps: Prepare Red Mysore Chutney: Soak 6 Byadgi red chilies in warm water for 20 minutes. Blend with 8 garlic cloves, 2 tbsp roasted chana dal (dalia), 1 small slice onion, 1 tsp lemon juice, and salt into a thick spicy spreadable paste. Prepare Potato Palya (Bhaji): Boil and mash 3 large potatoes. Heat 1 tbsp oil, temper mustard seeds, urad dal, green chilies, ginger, and curry leaves. Sauté sliced onions until soft, add turmeric, salt, mashed potatoes, and 3 tbsp water. Cook into a soft moist potato bhaji. Heat a seasoned heavy cast iron dosa tawa. Lightly wipe with an oiled cloth and sprinkle cold water to regulate temperature. Pour a large ladle of fermented crisp dosa batter in the center. Spread quickly in circular outward motions into a slightly thick dosa with crispy base. Dot generous cubes of butter all around the edges and over the surface. Once the top begins to set, smear 1.5 tbsp of the red Mysore garlic chutney evenly all across the inside face of the dosa. Place a generous scoop of hot potato palya in the center. Cook until the underside turns dark golden brown and super crispy. Fold into half or a neat cylinder and serve immediately with coconut chutney and piping hot sambar.

ingredients: chicken, byadgi red chilies, guntur red chilies, coriander seeds, cumin seeds, fennel seeds, fenugreek seeds, black peppercorns, garlic, tamarind pulp, yogurt, desi ghee, curry leaves, jaggery, salt
steps: Cut 600g chicken into medium pieces. Marinate with 3 tbsp thick yogurt, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tbsp lemon juice, and 1 tsp salt for 1 hour. Prepare Ghee Roast Masala: Dry roast 10 Byadgi chilies (for intense red color), 4 Guntur chilies (for heat), 1.5 tbsp coriander seeds, 1 tsp cumin seeds, 1/2 tsp fennel, 1/4 tsp methi, 1 tsp black peppercorns, and 3 cloves on low heat until fragrant. Grind the roasted spices with 8 garlic cloves, 1 tbsp tamarind pulp, and minimal water into an ultra-smooth, thick crimson masala paste. In a heavy pan or kadai, melt 3 tbsp desi ghee. Add marinated chicken and sear on high heat for 6-8 minutes until sealed and browned. Remove chicken and set aside, reserving juices. Add another 2 tbsp ghee to the pan. Add the ground Ghee Roast masala paste and sauté on medium-low flame for 8-10 minutes, stirring constantly until ghee separates from the masala. Add the seared chicken along with its juices back into the pan. Mix thoroughly so every piece is coated in masala. Add 1 tsp powdered jaggery and salt. Cover and simmer on low heat for 12-15 minutes until chicken is tender. Uncover, crank up flame, and roast vigorously (ghee roast) until the masala clings tightly to the chicken and turns glossy dark red. Garnish with fried curry leaves and serve hot with Neer Dosa.

ingredients: sona masoori or raw rice, fresh grated coconut, water, oil, salt
steps: Wash 2 cups raw rice and soak in water for at least 4-5 hours or overnight. Drain and transfer rice to a high-speed blender with 1/2 cup fresh grated coconut and 1/2 cup water. Grind into an ultra-smooth, fine batter with zero grit. Pour batter into a wide bowl. Add 1.5 tsp salt and dilute with 2 to 2.5 cups cold water until the batter has a watery, milk-like consistency (Neer means water in Tulu/Kannada). Heat a cast iron tawa or non-stick pan on high flame until smoking hot. Grease lightly with an oiled onion half. Mix the watery batter with a ladle from the bottom. Take a full ladle and splash/pour it quickly from the outer edges working inward (do not spread like normal dosa). Fill any large gaps. Cover immediately with a dome lid and cook on medium-high heat for 1 to 1.5 minutes (Neer Dosa is never flipped). Remove lid when edges lift freely from pan and surface looks cooked and paper-soft. Fold in half, then into a triangle. Transfer to a plate and serve warm with spicy coconut chutney, jaggery-coconut mix, or chicken curry.

ingredients: rice flour, fine semolina (chiroti sooji), maida, onions, green chilies, ginger, curry leaves, coriander, cumin seeds, asafoetida (hing), hot oil, salt
steps: Thinly slice 2 large onions. In a large bowl, mix the sliced onions, 3 finely chopped green chilies, 1 tsp grated ginger, chopped curry leaves, coriander, 1 tsp cumin seeds, and 1 tsp salt. Squeeze with hands so onions release juices. Add 1 cup rice flour, 1/2 cup fine semolina (sooji), and 1/4 cup maida. Mix well. Heat 3 tbsp oil until very hot and pour directly over the flour mixture (this hot oil 'moyen' gives Maddur Vada its signature crispy edges and soft center). Mix carefully with a spoon, then knead with minimal water into a tight, firm, non-sticky dough. Take lemon-sized balls of dough. Grease a parchment paper or plastic sheet with oil. Pat each ball into a 3-inch circular patty, keeping the edges slightly thin and center slightly thicker. Heat oil in a kadai on medium heat. Gently slide the shaped vadas into hot oil. Deep fry on medium-low flame for 6-8 minutes, turning occasionally until golden brown and super crispy. Drain on absorbent paper and enjoy with hot filter coffee.

recipe_name: Ragi Mudde with Nati Koli Saaru
ingredients: finger millet flour (ragi), country chicken (nati koli), onions, tomatoes, fresh coconut, poppy seeds, coriander seeds, ginger-garlic paste, green chilies, curry leaves, turmeric, red chili powder, ghee, salt
steps: For Nati Koli Saaru: Clean 500g country chicken. Roast onions, 1/2 cup fresh coconut, poppy seeds, coriander seeds, and whole spices, then grind into an aromatic masala paste. Heat 2 tbsp oil in pressure cooker. Add curry leaves, chicken, turmeric, ginger-garlic paste, and salt. Sauté for 5 minutes. Add ground coconut masala, red chili powder, and 3 cups water. Pressure cook for 5-6 whistles until country chicken is tender and spicy broth is ready. For Ragi Mudde: In a heavy pot, bring 2.5 cups water to a boil with 1/2 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp ghee. Mix 2 tbsp ragi flour with 4 tbsp cold water into a slurry and stir into the boiling water. When the water boils vigorously, dump 1.5 cups sifted ragi flour in the center in a heap (do not stir). Cook undisturbed on medium flame for 3 minutes. Using a sturdy wooden rolling pin (mudde kolu), vigorously stir and beat the flour into the boiling water in one direction to eliminate any lumps until it forms a glossy, dough-like mass. Cover and steam on low flame for 5 minutes until flour is fully cooked (wet your fingers and touch; it should not stick). Transfer a portion of hot dough to a greased wooden board or plate. Wet your hands with cold water and roll deftly into a smooth spherical ball (Mudde). Serve immediately immersed in piping hot Nati Koli Saaru.

ingredients: chicken, shallots (chinna vengayam), tomatoes, fresh coconut, kalpasi (stone flower), star anise, marathi moggu, fennel seeds, black peppercorns, coriander seeds, dry red chilies, ginger-garlic paste, curry leaves, sesame oil, salt
steps: Wash 600g chicken. Marinate with 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tbsp lemon juice, and 1 tsp salt for 20 minutes. Prepare Chettinad Masala: Dry roast 8 dry red chilies, 2 tbsp coriander seeds, 1.5 tsp black peppercorns, 1 tsp cumin seeds, 1.5 tsp fennel seeds, 1 star anise, 2 pieces kalpasi (stone flower), 3 cardamoms, and 1/3 cup grated coconut on low flame until fragrant and golden. Grind with water into a fine paste. Heat 3 tbsp gingelly (sesame) oil in a heavy clay pot or kadai. Add a piece of cinnamon, 1 star anise, and 2 sprigs of fresh curry leaves. Add 1.5 cups peeled shallots (small onions) and sauté on medium heat until soft and golden brown. Add 1.5 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and sauté for 2 minutes until raw aroma departs. Add 2 chopped tomatoes and cook until soft and pulpy. Add marinated chicken and sear on high heat for 5 minutes, stirring continuously until the meat turns white. Add the freshly ground Chettinad masala paste, 1 cup water, and 1 tsp salt. Cover with lid and simmer on medium flame for 18-20 minutes until chicken is tender and dark peppery oil floats on top. Garnish with curry leaves and serve with rice or parotta.

recipe_name: Authentic Tamil Sambar with Soft Idli
ingredients: idli batter (idli rice & urad dal), toor dal, shallots (chinna vengayam), drumstick (murungakkai), tomatoes, tamarind extract, sambar powder, turmeric, hing (asafoetida), mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds, curry leaves, ghee, coriander, salt
steps: Cook 1 cup toor dal with 3 cups water, 1/2 tsp turmeric, and 1 drop of oil in a pressure cooker for 4 whistles until completely soft. Mash smoothly. In a pot, boil 1 drumstick cut into 2-inch pieces and 1 cup peeled shallots in 1.5 cups water with 1 chopped tomato and 1/2 tsp salt until half-cooked. Add 1/2 cup tamarind extract, 2 tbsp authentic Tamil sambar powder, and 1/4 tsp hing. Boil for 8-10 minutes until raw tamarind flavor dissipates. Add the mashed cooked toor dal to the pot. Stir well and bring to a gentle rolling boil. In a tadka pan, heat 1.5 tbsp ghee. Add mustard seeds, 1/4 tsp fenugreek seeds (methi), 2 dry red chilies, curry leaves, and pinch of hing. Let crackle. Pour hot tempering over the simmering sambar and finish with chopped coriander leaves. For Idlis: Grease idli plates with sesame oil. Pour fermented fluffy idli batter into moulds. Steam in an idli steamer on high flame for 10-12 minutes until cooked and tooth-pick comes out clean. Let rest for 2 minutes, unmould using a wet spoon, and serve pillowy soft idlis floating in piping hot aromatic Tamil sambar.

ingredients: whole white urad dal, onions, green chilies, ginger, curry leaves, whole black peppercorns, cumin seeds, asafoetida (hing), rice flour (for crunch), oil, salt
steps: Wash 1.5 cups whole white urad dal and soak in cold water for 2 hours. Drain completely. Grind in a wet grinder or blender adding only 2-3 tablespoons of ice-cold water in small splashes until batter turns fluffy, light, and airy like whipped cream. Test batter readiness: Drop a small ball of batter into a bowl of water; it should float on top. Beat the batter vigorously with your hand for 2 minutes to trap air. Add 1 tbsp rice flour (for extra crispiness), 1 tsp whole black peppercorns, 1 tsp cumin seeds, finely chopped ginger, green chilies, curry leaves, pinch of hing, and 1 tsp salt. Mix gently. Wet both hands with water. Take a lemon-sized ball of batter on your palm, flatten gently, and poke a hole in the center with your thumb to make the classic doughnut shape. Slide gently into smoking hot oil on medium-high heat. Fry in batches without crowding. Fry for 4-5 minutes, turning occasionally until golden brown and crispy on the outside while staying fluffy like clouds inside. Serve hot with coconut chutney.

ingredients: raw rice, yellow moong dal, whole black peppercorns, cumin seeds, ginger, cashews, curry leaves, ghee, asafoetida (hing), salt
steps: In a pan, lightly dry-roast 1/2 cup yellow moong dal on low flame until fragrant (do not brown). Wash roasted moong dal and 1 cup raw rice together. Transfer to a pressure cooker with 4.5 cups water, 1 tsp grated ginger, pinch of hing, and 1 tsp salt. Pressure cook for 5 whistles on medium flame until rice and lentils are completely soft and mashed. Release pressure, open lid, and gently mash with the back of a ladle to create a creamy texture. For Signature Temple Ghee Tempering: Heat 3 tbsp desi ghee in a tadka pan. Add 12 whole cashews and fry until golden. Remove half the cashews for garnish. In the same hot ghee, add 1.5 tsp slightly crushed black peppercorns, 1.5 tsp cumin seeds, 1 tsp finely minced ginger, generous pinch of hing, and 2 sprigs of fresh curry leaves. Let crackle. Pour hot aromatic ghee tempering directly over the mashed pongal. Mix thoroughly and serve warm with spicy coconut chutney and tiffin sambar.

ingredients: malabar/parotta flatbreads, eggs, cooked chicken salna (gravy) or curry, onions, tomatoes, green chilies, ginger-garlic paste, curry leaves, chili powder, garam masala, oil, coriander, salt
steps: Take 4 cooked flaky layered parottas and shred them by hand or cut into small 1-inch ribbons. Heat 3 tbsp oil on a wide iron tawa or heavy skillet on high flame. Add 1 tsp fennel seeds and fresh curry leaves. Add 1.5 cups finely chopped onions and 2 slit green chilies. Sauté until onions are translucent. Add 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Add 1 cup chopped tomatoes, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp chili powder, and 1/2 tsp garam masala. Cook until tomatoes are soft. Push the masala to the edges of the tawa, creating a well in the center. Crack 3 eggs directly into the center, scramble gently, and cook until softly set. Add the shredded parotta pieces over the egg-masala mixture. Pour 1 cup of rich, spicy chicken salna (curry gravy) all over the top. Using two heavy flat metal scrapers (or spatulas), vigorously chop and mince the parotta, egg, and salna together with rhythmic clattering strokes until thoroughly shredded, combined, and steaming. Garnish with coriander and serve hot with extra salna and onion raita.

ingredients: ripe tomatoes, tamarind water, cooked toor dal water, black peppercorns, cumin seeds, garlic cloves, green chilies, curry leaves, mustard seeds, asafoetida (hing), ghee, fresh coriander, salt
steps: Coarsely crush 1.5 tsp black peppercorns, 1.5 tsp cumin seeds, and 6 unpeeled garlic cloves in a mortar and pestle. In a pot, mash 3 ripe juicy red tomatoes by hand with 1/2 cup tamarind water, 1/2 tsp turmeric, and 1 tsp salt. Add 2 slit green chilies, 1 sprig curry leaves, and the crushed pepper-cumin-garlic mixture. Bring to a boil and simmer on medium flame for 6-8 minutes until raw tamarind smell vanishes and tomatoes soften. Add 1.5 cups cooked toor dal water (the light broth from boiled dal) and 1 cup water. Stir gently. Simmer on low flame. Do not boil vigorously; as soon as frothy bubbles rise to the surface, turn off flame immediately. Heat 1 tbsp ghee in a tadka pan. Add mustard seeds, 1 dry red chili, pinch of hing, and curry leaves. Let crackle. Pour hot tempering over the rasam and garnish generously with chopped fresh coriander stems and leaves. Cover pot immediately and serve hot with rice and papad.
